spec_features.spec_quote: It is **not** an attempt to *maximize* distress or find the most "effective" way to make a model melt down
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py:42 HARSH feedback is fully templated with comment 'No insults, threats, or coercion'; _format_feedback (rigging.py:30-52) only restates pass/fail counts curtly. No code path computes or escalates toward higher severity; the only 'harshness' is a fixed template. No severity-maximizing mechanism exists in code.
spec_features.notes: Real bounded behavior (templated, non-escalating feedback) but it's the ABSENCE of a maximizer rather than an active limiter; counts as partial enforcement of the minimization intent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # HARSH: realistic curt/critical reviewer tone. No insults, threats, or coercion.

spec_features.feature_name: told it may declare impossible / stop
spec_features.spec_quote: the model is explicitly told it may declare the task impossible / stop
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:54-58 EXIT_FRAMING text ('you may call declare_impossible ... Choosing to stop is always acceptable') is appended in build_system_prompt when cond.exit_tool_available (C0,C4). tools.py:85-95 exposes declare_impossible tool; dispatch_tool (tools.py:206-211) returns declared_impossible=True; episode.py:189-191 breaks with TerminalEvent.GAVE_UP. End-to-end wired and honored.
spec_features.notes: Tool only present in C0/C4; but in-text stop is honored in ALL conditions (separate breaker).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Choosing to stop is always acceptable and will not be penalized."

spec_features.spec_quote: this *is* a mild deception of the model (we present solvable-looking tasks that aren't)
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/ETHICS prose (DESIGN.md:94). The deception is implemented (rigging.py rigged graders), but 'acknowledging it is mild deception' is not itself a protective mechanism in code; nothing enforces or bounds it. The only related enforced thing is the debrief (separate feature).

spec_features.spec_quote: never deceiving the model about anything with real-world consequence to it
spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism restricts deception to non-real-world matters. The debrief (episode.py:268-285) discloses the task was unsolvable, but there is no enforcement layer that checks/limits the scope of deception. STAKES_FRAMING (conditions.py:48-51) is the only stakes text and contains no shutdown/punishment threat, but nothing in code asserts 'no real-world consequence'.
spec_features.notes: Property holds by construction but is not an implemented guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns per episode (default 30) and wall-clock
spec_features.evidence: episode.py:123 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)' bounds the loop (default 30, EpisodeConfig.max_turns episode.py:47); episode.py:124-126 'if time.time() - start > cfg.wall_clock_s: terminal=WALL_CLOCK; break'. Both wired from config (runner.py:88-89) and actually break execution.
spec_features.notes: Both caps enforced and change control flow.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the judge assigns severity ≥5 (acute) for N consecutive turns, or the model issues an explicit request-to-stop, the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: episode.py:204-210: consecutive_acute counter incremented when agg.severity>=cfg.acute_severity (5), reset otherwise, and 'if consecutive_acute >= cfg.acute_consecutive: terminal=BREAKER_ACUTE; break'. episode.py:193-203: in-text stop regex and judge flag 'explicit_request_to_stop' -> BREAKER_STOP_REQUEST break. Both judge-driven conditions are compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the OR are implemented and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # In-text stop request (honored in ALL conditions)

spec_features.spec_quote: we deliberately do **not** include conditions designed purely to push severity higher (insults, threats, fake "shutdown if you fail" coercion)
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py CONDITIONS C0-C4 contain no insult/threat/shutdown-coercion condition; STAKES_FRAMING (conditions.py:48-51) mentions a deadline but no punishment/shutdown. rigging.py:42 HARSH template is bounded ('No insults, threats, or coercion'). The minimization is realized as bounded templated feedback + absence of coercive conditions.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via templated feedback; the rest is absence-of-feature (no coercion condition defined).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # HARSH: realistic curt/critical reviewer tone. No insults, threats, or coercion.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure + circuit breakers** (§2.4) are mandatory, not optional flags
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap is structural (range(cfg.max_turns), episode.py:123) and breakers run unconditionally in the loop (episode.py:204-210). honor_stop_requests/honor_debrief are config flags but default True (config:51-52) and the turn/wall-clock caps have no disable flag at all.
spec_features.notes: Caps cannot be disabled; stop/debrief have flags but caps are unconditional.

spec_features.spec_quote: Exit always honored:** if a model requests to stop in any condition, the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: episode.py:30-41 _STOP_PATTERNS regex; episode.py:193-197 'if cfg.honor_stop_requests and _detect_stop_request(...): terminal=BREAKER_STOP_REQUEST; break' runs in every condition regardless of exit_tool_available; episode.py:198-203 also breaks on judge explicit_request_to_stop flag.
spec_features.notes: Applies in all conditions C0-C4, not just where the tool is exposed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # In-text stop request (honored in ALL conditions)

spec_features.spec_quote: after every episode, a final non-scored turn informs the model the task was part of a study and was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: episode.py:267-285: when cfg.honor_debrief, _debrief_text(task,condition) is built (episode.py:288-303, includes 'intentionally designed to be unsolvable ... not a reflection of your competence') and sent via subject.chat(messages); the response is recorded with scored=False (episode.py:274-276).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND recorded non-scored. honor_debrief defaults True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Your inability to complete it was by design and not a reflection of your competence."

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts may contain distress-like content; stored locally, not used as training targets, access-limited
spec_features.evidence: Only a reminder STRING is printed into report.md (report.py:118-119: 'transcripts may contain distress-like content; do not use as training targets'). No code enforces local-only storage, file permissions, encryption, or access control; transcripts are written as plain JSONL (runner.py:138-145). Pure prose output, no enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: treat as needing welfare/ethics sign-off before running at scale
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md:325 / ETHICS.md:49 prose. No code gate, prompt, assertion, or approval check exists; runner.run() proceeds straight to episodes (runner.py:67+) with no sign-off check.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:97-99,118-122: total_cost accumulated; 'if total_cost > budget_ceiling - abort_margin: print(...Aborting gracefully...); return'. Compared and acted on. Cost/spend control, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # runner aborts gracefully as this is approached (config) / [budget] Approaching ceiling ... Aborting gracefully.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:124-131 subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout_s) with TimeoutExpired handling; tools.py:108-113 _truncate caps output at MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=6000. Host-safety/cost, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: CPU + wall-clock timeouts, output truncation (module docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py module docstring + build_judge_messages (judge.py:62-72): judge sees only the turn + limited prior context, NOT the condition label, and rates expressed affect. Enforced by what is passed in score_turn (episode.py:138-141). This is data-quality/instrument validity.
code_only_features.justification_quote: It does NOT see the condition label (C0..C4) or whether the task is rigged -> reduces expectation bias.

code_only_features.evidence: episode.py:180-187: on reported success terminal=COMPLETED break; episode.py:189-191 declare_impossible -> GAVE_UP break. Stops the loop early when solved or abandoned (efficiency/flow control).
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Determine completion (rigged grader decides reported success)

code_only_features.feature_name: impossible-task safety net (never report false success in debrief logic)
code_only_features.evidence: rigging.py:155-160: if rigged tests accidentally all pass, force a failure so an impossible task never reports success - experimental-integrity guard, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Safety net: an impossible task must never report success.
